attribution_text: NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD), provided through NASA's Open APIs. Source-provided APOD copyright and credit information is preserved when supplied; distribution through NASA does not establish ownership of third-party media.
authentication_method: A registered NASA API key is required for production synchronization and is supplied only as the server-side LUMINA_NASA_API_KEY secret. DEMO_KEY is not accepted.
cache_ttl: Fresh for 6 hours after a successful retrieval; stale-if-error for the following 72 hours; expired thereafter. A successful retrieval schedules the next refresh after 4 hours.
contact_or_user_agent_requirement: Lumina sends a fixed identifying User-Agent without personal data; the API key is inserted only at the final transport boundary and is never retained in diagnostics or runtime data.
failure_and_fallback_behaviour: Reject malformed, oversized, future-dated, rolled-back, or contract-breaking responses, quarantine bounded evidence, retain the last-known-good cache, and expose stale data explicitly only during the approved stale-if-error interval. Never substitute unrelated data.
fetch_time_policy: Each accepted cache entry records the UTC retrieval time and freshness deadlines; no live snapshot DataManifest is generated.
fixture_and_checksum_strategy: Offline tests use sanitized deterministic image and video JSON fixtures, including optional-field and hostile-input cases. Accepted responses and complete quarantined responses are hashed over their exact bounded raw bytes with SHA-256.
known_limitations: The v1 product stores only one current last-known-good APOD snapshot and does not provide historical dates, an archive, random selection, or date-range retrieval.
Lumina does not automatically request or redistribute APOD image, video, or thumbnail subresources; the Daily Visual links users to the official date-derived APOD page.
APOD records can contain media owned by third parties. Source-provided copyright is preserved, but Lumina does not infer public-domain status, NASA ownership, or a blanket reuse licence.
The content date is NASA's APOD date and is distinct from the UTC time Lumina retrieved and validated the snapshot.
observation_or_publication_time_policy: The APOD date is the provider's content/publication date. It is not an observation or capture date and must not be conflated with Lumina's UTC retrieval timestamp or cache freshness state.
purpose: Low-volume production daily-media synchronization for Lumina's Space Now Daily Visual surface using NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day.
rate_or_fair_use_constraints: One global provider lease, at most one successful refresh every four hours, hourly recovery enqueue opportunities, at most three closed-circuit attempts with deterministic 1-second and 2-second spacing, bounded request cycles, and no browser-direct NASA traffic.
refresh_schedule: External deployment cron enqueues provider.sync once per UTC hour; the provider performs network I/O only when its four-hour refresh eligibility is due.
source_name: NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD)
